propositions: Review-bot uvicorn access logs record the full request line including query parameters, exposing the webhook token in plaintext to journald and any log consumers.
The webhook secret is configured as GERRIT_BOT_TOKEN and serves as the authentication credential for both /webhook and /rerun endpoints, making its exposure a privilege escalation risk.
The plaintext token persists in journald, log excerpts shared in tickets and chats, and any log-shipping infrastructure without user awareness or alarming, creating a fail-open exposure.

The fix moves the token from query string to X-Rebar-Token HTTP header (not recorded in access logs) with TokenRedactingFilter as a redaction backstop, while maintaining observability for route and status logging.
The previously-logged GERRIT_BOT_TOKEN must be rotated independently and the rotation explicitly recorded, as the code fix alone does not un-leak credentials already written to journald.
